facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s with recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
presented with a pruritic rash ongoing for 2 weeks
The rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
then gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
She denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Erythematous annular plaques without scale on her right arm and bilateral legs
4-mm punch biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain was negative for fungal organisms
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating numerous scattered eosinophils

concepts.why: The patient developed a pruritic rash after initiation of immunotherapy, which is a known side effect of such treatments.
The biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils support this diagnosis.
The histopathology results demonstrate perivascular inflammation, which is a key feature of this condition.
The patient's symptoms of a pruritic rash and erythematous annular plaques are consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms of a pruritic rash and erythematous annular plaques could also be consistent with atopic dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms of erythematous annular plaques could be consistent with psoriasis, although the absence of scale makes this less likely.
The patient's symptoms of erythematous annular plaques could be consistent with lichen planus, although the absence of other characteristic features makes this less likely.
The patient's symptoms of a pruritic rash developed after initiation of immunotherapy, which could be a drug rash.
The presence of numerous eosinophils and negative PAS stain for fungal organisms explains the uncovered fact of eosinophilic inflammation.
